data.content_ref: inline:The target proposes a strict cascade of progressively stronger causal-decorrelation tests, yet never identifies the causal mechanism that forces each level to depend on the prior: it asserts that higher-level checks 'verify' lower-level signals, but provides no mechanism explaining why a decorrelated signal lacking refutation capacity would fail, or why perturbation sensitivity without population statistics is causally insufficient. Without such a mechanism, the levels could be independent evidence streams rather than a cascade, which makes the proposed integration relation (cascade/dependence) unsupported.
